I recently visited Third Wave Coffee and ordered a French Press. One of the reasons I chose this brewing method was because I enjoy the complete coffee experience, including the final plunge before serving. (Any other coffee brand in the city allows you to do this on your own)
I politely requested if I could do the plunge myself, but the staff member in charge refused. Even after I explained that I was genuinely interested in the process, I was not given a clear reason for the denial. If there are safety or company policies that prevent customers from participating, those should be communicated transparently rather than dismissed without explanation.
What made the experience even more frustrating was the service speed. Despite ordering a French Press, I had to wait over 30 minutes to receive my coffee. For a beverage that was prepared on-site, the wait felt excessive, especially given the lack of communication or updates from the staff.
The combination of the unexplained refusal and the extremely long wait left me disappointed. Specialty coffee is about more than just the drink—it is about customer engagement, hospitality, and the overall experience. Unfortunately, this visit fell short on all three fronts.
I hope Third Wave Coffee takes customer feedback seriously and works on improving both service efficiency and customer interaction. A little transparency and attentiveness would go a long way toward creating a better experience.

featured_reviews.name: Perpetual Gomes
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Slow in Kandivli recently with my cousin sister, and honestly, while the food and coffee were good, the overall experience and service left us extremely uncomfortable.

When we entered, there were multiple empty 4-seater tables available (which remained empty throughout most of our visit), yet we were seated at their “community table”  which is essentially a tiny circular table against the wall that is genuinely not practical for two people ordering food and drinks.

One of the waiters later moved us to a proper table after realizing the issue, but shortly after, someone managing the cafe asked the waiter to move us back to the tiny community table again. We even mentioned that it would be difficult to comfortably eat there once food arrived, but were told “it will be fine.”

Unfortunately, it really wasn’t.

Things kept falling while we were eating because there simply wasn’t enough space. We had to move the cutlery setup ourselves just to make room for the plates and drinks. Nobody checked in or offered any solution despite clearly seeing the inconvenience.

What honestly made the experience worse was noticing another individual sitting alone with camera equipment/content setup being comfortably given a larger table while we, as paying customers ordering food and coffee, were repeatedly denied one despite tables remaining vacant throughout our meal.

If the cafe had been full, this would’ve been understandable. But it wasn’t.

The food itself was genuinely good and reasonably priced, which makes this more disappointing because the experience could have been great with just basic consideration and hospitality.

Also adding a service charge after this experience honestly felt a little absurd.

I hope the cafe improves how they treat regular customers moving forward because good food alone isn’t enough to make people return.

featured_reviews.name: Pragya Singh

TLDR: Good ambience, (at best) average Food, terrible beverages. Overpriced disappointment!

We were genuinely excited to visit the place and had already returned twice because of the waiting earlier but God were we disappointed! Biggest let down was the signature cold chocolate which was just a sugary syrup and a disgrace to be called 55% dark chocolate. It tasted like drinking sweet flour (probably to make it thicker). Felt so bad about the extra calories and 400 bucks going down the drain for this whereas a small sachet of Tiggle does a WAYYY better job at home. I even requested the server if I could get a stronger version of chocolate by tweaking it after having just one sip but he refused by saying that the jaggery/palm sugar already comes mixed with the chocolate so there's nothing they can do about it.
The burrito bowl was average, not bad but nothing I'd go again for. And the nachos were a bit stale, so much for "fresh and from scratch" ingredients.
The broccoli and cottage cheese burger didn't feel like it had any cottage cheese but rather just broccoli and mushed potatoes. The hand cut fries that came with it were too salty, oily and soggy.
Lastly, the spiced orange cream iced latte only sounded fancy and had cream chunks instead of a well frothed foam on top.
The only good parts were that the ambience has been tastefully decorated and the service is quick.

featured_reviews.name: Priyank Mehta
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited Cafe Town on a Sunday evening for a quick snack, but ended up trying quite a few items (pictures attached).

We ordered loaded nachos, pink sauce pasta, veg steamed momos, a Nutella shake, and a cold hazelnut coffee.

To be honest, nothing really stood out. Most of the items were below average — I would rate them around 3/10. The only relatively better dish was the pink sauce pasta, which I would rate around 5/10 — decent, but nothing exceptional.

The loaded nachos were quite disappointing. They didn’t feel “loaded” at all — just some chopped onions, capsicum, and tomatoes sprinkled on top with grated cheese and mayo. Definitely not worth the money.

The momos were okay taste-wise, but didn’t feel like value for money — only 5 pieces for the price didn’t justify it.

Coming to the beverages, they were very disappointing. The cold coffee was excessively sweet and not properly mixed. The Nutella shake was even worse — the Nutella wasn’t blended properly, and I could literally feel chunks/paste of it coming through the straw, which ruined the experience.

Overall, it was quite an underwhelming visit and not something I would strongly recommend.
